name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Add a mandatory prompt review step at the start of every task. This forces us to verify the prompt’s clarity, scope, and constraints before execution, cutting wasted work from misaligned inputs. The trade-off is a small upfront time cost, but it prevents larger rework later. Without this, we risk solving the wrong problem or missing critical constraints.

name: Gauge
text: Mandatory prompt review risks review fatigue where reviewers gloss over prompts after the 10th task, turning a safeguard into a checkbox. Instead, automate a lightweight pre-check that flags only high-risk prompts (e.g., vague scope, missing constraints) for human review—this cuts wasted work without creating a new bottleneck. Settle this by running a 2-week pilot: compare rework rates and reviewer satisfaction with and without the automation.
